Hō^ra , ae, f. perh. an old form for hĕra, lady,
I.the wife of Quirinus (Romulus), who was worshipped as a goddess (called, before her death, Hersilia, Ov. M. 14, 830): Quirine pater, veneror, Horamque Quirini, Enn. ap. Non. 120, 2 (Ann. v. 121 Vahl.): “Hora Quirini,” Gell. 13, 22, 2 ; cf.: “pariter cum corpore nomen Mutat Horamque vocat,” Ov. M. 14, 851 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
